newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian premier says Taiwan office to close.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian premier says Taiwan office to close.

text.p: Cambodian co-premier Hun Sen said on Tuesday city authorities would close Taiwan's office in Cambodia because of its alleged involvement in backing forces loyal to ousted First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh.
Hun Sen, who ousted Ranariddh on July 6, said Taiwan investors were not involved in the affair and they should continue business as usual.
"Phnom Penh authorities have decided to close the representative office for Taiwan," Hun Sen told a meeting of foreign investors.
Earlier, Hun Sen said unidentified Taiwanese, including a general, supported Ranariddh's forces before fighting erupted between troops loyal to the two premiers on July 5.
"It is not revenge, but just a measure to find out who is involved in this incident," he said.
"A general came to Phnom Penh through this office." He did not elaborate, but said the office had one week to close.
An official at Taiwan's Economic and Cultural Representative Office in Phnom Penh said the office had yet to be officially informed of the decision but he thought the move might be only temporary.
Taipei has denied any involvement of Taiwan people in supporting Ranariddh's forces.
Taiwan is the biggest foreign investor in Cambodia and Hun Sen said Taiwan companies should continue to operate as normal.
"The Taiwanese companies here were not involved at all, and they are advised to carry on as normal," he said. "This incident in no way involves investors from Taipei."
Hun Sen said Beijing's embassy in Phnom Penh was sufficient to look after the interests of Chinese people in Cambodia.
"The embassy of the People's Republic of China is enough to provide protection for Chinese people," Hun Sen said.
Cambodia follows a one-China policy and maintains diplomatic relations with Beijing. Nationalist forces set up a rival government on Taiwan after losing a civil war in 1949.
